page.layout: One text column on the right of the page, with a narrow left margin holding one marginal note ("LOCVS.") beside the first paragraph of the chapter. Running head at the top, catchword at the right foot below the last line.

p.i: At Quies, si est privatio motus in subiecto, ad eum ex natura sua apto, potest esse naturalis à principio interno: à principio externo violen-tus.

main_text.head: CAPUT QUARTUM. DE LOCO ET TEMPORE.
main_text.p: LOCVS.Entitas & circumscriptio est affectio corporis communis, 'qua corpus suis continetur terminis, (scilicet Loci aut temporis.
Omne enim corpus naturale est finitum & circumscriptum.

p.i: Nota. Ut quaedam mutabilitas & motus tribui potest mentibus ac Spiritibus creatis: ita etiam finitum esse, competit omni creaturae tam spirituali, quam corporeae. Ideoq; mutabilitas & finitas latius patent corpore naturali.

main_text.p: Omne quippe corpus est quantum. Quanti vero affectio est corporea finitudo, & circumscriptio.
Est vero corpus Physicum finitum & circumscriptum tùm Loco, tùm Tem-pore.

page.notes: The large woodcut initial is an ornamented E, read as the first letter of "Entitas". The apostrophe in "'qua" is printed as shown. Faint show-through of the facing page is visible in both margins and across the text area; it is not transcribed. Faint "B 2" and "Sca" fragments at the foot are show-through and are left out, so there is no signature. The left-margin note "LOCVS." is the only printed marginal note.
